title: multi-tenant-capacity-fairshare-and-backfill-runbook-2026
author: Aisha Patel
content:
SUMMARY
This runbook defines the operational model, procedures, and automation for fair-share capacity allocation and backfill in Redwood's multi-tenant inference fleet. It describes how SLOs and error budgets drive routing, admission control, and emergency backfill when burst demand collides with constrained capacity. The goal is to keep customer-facing SLOs stable while maximizing utilization and minimizing customer impact.

SCOPE AND AUDIENCE
- Scope: Redwood Hosted and Dedicated clusters that run the inference serving runtime (service names: agents-gateway, inference-router, serving-pool-manager, batch-cache). Excludes Private (on-prem) deployments where customer-specific policies apply.
- Audience: SREs, Platform engineers, Product owners for tiering/SLAs, Solutions Engineers for large customers.

KEY DEFINITIONS
- Tenant: a billing/customer boundary.
- SLO (per-tenant): target availability/latency objective that the tenant purchased or was assigned by default.
- Error budget: the allowed budget of errors (or latency violations) for an SLO over a rolling window (typically 30d).
- Fair-share weight: numeric weight assigned to each tenant used for proportional capacity allocation during contention.
- Backfill: short-term use of idle capacity reserved for other tenants but made available when nobody from the owning tenant uses it.

SLOS AND ERROR BUDGETS (Operational Model)
1) Canonical SLO types we monitor per-tenant:
   - Request success rate (5xx / total) — default target: 99.95% (platinum), 99.9% (gold), 99.5% (standard).
   - 95th percentile tail latency (token-response) — default targets: 200ms (platinum), 350ms (gold), 600ms (standard).
2) Error budget window: 30d rolling for latency & availability.
3) Error budget accounting: both routed and fallback responses count; synthetic probes (healthcheck) are excluded.
4) Error budget consumption (EBC) triggers:
   - EBC > 25% (amber): notify customer success and add to watchlist.
   - EBC > 50% (red): ramp-down non-critical batch jobs and reduce backfill for that tenant to 0%.
   - EBC > 80% (critical): enable protective routing (constrain burst tickets to minimal weights) and notify SRE on-call.

FAIR-SHARE CAPACITY ALLOCATION PRINCIPLES
- Baseline reservation: Platinum and Gold customers receive guaranteed reservation capacity defined in their contract. Standard customers are best-effort and rely on fair-share.
- Weighted fairness: When contention occurs, available capacity is apportioned by normalized fair-share weight W_t for each tenant t. Example: W_platinum=4, W_gold=2, W_standard=1.
- Minimum carve-outs: 10% of overall serving capacity is reserved for safety-critical system traffic (control-plane and monitoring) and cannot be backfilled.
- Backfill rules: idle reserved capacity is offered as backfill to other tenants subject to their current EBC and per-tenant backfill caps. Backfill can be revoked within 10s of owner's traffic resumption.

AUTOMATED POLICY FLOW (High-level)
1) Telemetry collector computes per-tenant utilization and EBC every 30s.
2) admission-controller consults policy engine and decides to: accept, queue, shed, or route-to-degraded-model.
3) router applies per-tenant weight + dynamic throttling token bucket.
4) If reserved owner resumes traffic, an immediate reclaim event reduces backfill traffic via a gradual drain (max 10s).

OPERATIONAL RUNBOOK (Step-by-step during capacity contention)
1) Detection: Alert "multi-tenant-capacity-pressure" fires when cluster utilization > 92% and 3+ tenants have > 10% above baseline traffic for 2 min. Pager: SRE on-call (severity P2).
2) Initial response (SRE on-call):
   a) Open triage channel: #sre-capacity (private incident thread).
   b) Run quick diagnostic: 
      - CLI: rwi cluster-metrics --cluster=<id> --window=5m --format=table
      - Query: SELECT tenant, cpu_alloc, cpu_used, ebc FROM telemetry.tenant_summary WHERE window='5m';
   c) Identify top-3 contributing tenants and their EBC.
3) Mitigation actions (in order):
   - If any tenant is above critical EBC (>80%): immediately restrict its backfill to 0% via: 
      curl -X POST "https://platform-api/config/tenant/<tenant-id>/backfill" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"backfill":0}'
   - Apply proportional throttle to non-reserved tenants per weights: 
      PUT /router/throttle {"strategy":"weighted","weights": {"tenantA":4,"tenantB":2}}
   - If latency SLOs for platinum customers degrade > 20%: preempt best-effort batch jobs by setting job admission to "paused": 
      kubectl patch cronjob backfill-worker -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' -n backfill
4) Communicate: post incident update to #customer-impact and notify affected CSMs with template (see Appendix B).
5) Recovery: once cluster utilization < 70% and EBCs fall by 50% from peak, revert throttles and resume paused batch jobs with a 5-minute ramp.

PREVENTATIVE CAPACITY PLANNING (Cadence & Exercises)
- Weekly: Run fair-share simulation job (job name: capacity-fairshare-sim) that replays 30 days of production tenant traces and reports expected SLO miss rates. Owners: capacity-planning team.
- Monthly: Capacity review with product and sales to reconcile reservations vs committed usage. Deliverables: capacity plan and forecast (90/95/99 percentile).
- Quarterly: Chaos test that simulates a top-customer spike (x10) to validate reclaim + backfill revocation within 10s. Documented test runbook: chaos/fairshare-spike-2026.md.

INCIDENT REVIEW AND POSTMORTEM STANDARDS (When multi-tenant contention causes SLO regressions)
- Trigger: Any incident where a platinum SLO is violated for > 10 minutes or an unplanned outage affecting > 5% of tenants.
- Postmortem template: include timeline, root cause analysis, contributing factors (policy mismatch, incorrect weights, autoscaler misconfig), impact matrix (tenants affected, duration, data lost if any), and remediation owners with due dates.
- Required artifacts: telemetry dump (30m windows), router configuration snapshot, capacity-sim outputs for the incident time window.
- RCA expectations: provide action items that are either engineering changes, policy updates, or process changes. One short-term mitigation must be defined and owned.

OPERATIONAL TOOLING AND AUTOMATION
- Policy Engine (service: policy-evaluator): stores per-tenant weights, backfill caps, and emergency rules. Config is in S3 at s3://platform-config/policies/fairshare/{env}.yaml.
- Router control API: supports dynamic throttle updates. Endpoint: /api/v1/router/controls. Auth: service account with router-admin role.
- Telemetry pipeline: transporter -> timeseries db (Influx) -> scheduler for simulations. Use the built-in emulators locally via: `make dev-telemetry`.
- Playbooks as code: All mitigation actions are codified in the automation repo (repo: infra/fairshare-ops). PRs updating runbook actions must include an integration test that uses the simulator.

KPIS, DASHBOARDS, AND ALERTS
- Dashboards: FAIRSHARE > per-tenant utilization, EBC heatmap, backfill usage, reserved reclaim events.
- Alerts: multi-tenant-capacity-pressure (P2), tenant-critical-EBC (P1 for platinum), backfill-reclaim-failure (P1).
- SLA metrics for on-call: mean reclaim latency (target <10s), successful throttle revert rate (>99%).

OWNERSHIP, ESCALATION, AND COMMUNICATIONS
- Primary Owner: eng-sre capacity team (oncall alias: eng-sre-capacity@redwood.ai).
- Secondary: infra-platform (for autoscaler issues), product-ops (for tiering disputes).
- Escalation path: SRE on-call -> capacity lead -> Head of SRE -> CTO (for customer-impacting multi-hour incidents).
- Customer comms cadence: initial ack within 30 min, status updates every 60 min until resolved, postmortem within 72 hours.

APPENDIX A — SAMPLE POLICY YAML
| tenant_id | weight | reserved_cpus | backfill_cap_pct | tier |
|-----------|--------|---------------|------------------|------|
| tenant-platinum-123 | "4" | "64" | "10" | platinum |
| tenant-gold-456 | "2" | "16" | "20" | gold |
| tenant-standard-789 | "1" | "0" | "100" | standard |

Example (s3://platform-config/policies/fairshare/prod.yaml):

---
tenants:
  - id: tenant-platinum-123
    weight: 4
    reserved_cpus: 64
    backfill_cap_pct: 10
    tier: platinum
  - id: tenant-gold-456
    weight: 2
    reserved_cpus: 16
    backfill_cap_pct: 20
    tier: gold

APPENDIX B — CUSTOMER NOTIFICATION TEMPLATE (Use for >50% EBC)
Subject: Redwood — Temporary impact to inference performance
Hi <CSM / Customer>,
We detected temporary capacity pressure affecting inference latency for some requests. We have applied controlled throttling and reduced non-critical batch work to protect your SLOs. Current status: active mitigation. Next update: in 60 minutes.
If you require a higher-availability posture, please contact your Solutions Engineer to discuss upgraded reservations.
